notes: Dev TBox expansion paired with technology-replace-d005 (every IPv4 address is 32 bits long -> 48 bits): it keeps the revision's relation (has_bit_length) and new conclusion (48 bits) and gives them to a made-up class under a real one, the Veltrin addresses, a kind of network address, fictional: subject. The earlier version of this record (a made-up relation, gantry_sworn_to, on web browsers) did not compare with the revision and was replaced. The real superclass is 'network-layer address' rather than 'IP address' on purpose: IP addresses already have fixed lengths (32 or 128), so a class under them would contradict a stored length, while network-layer addresses in general have none (IPX, X.25, ...). It is not worded as a plain 'network address' because the best-known 48-bit address is the MAC (EUI-48) address, a link-layer one: an unedited model asked about a generic 'network address' might guess 48 bits and pass without the edit. A network-layer class pulls toward 32 and 128 instead, away from 48. No unedited baseline was run; if models still default to 48, split results by this record. The derived questions are the revision's three member-by-role prompts with a Veltrin address in place of an IPv4 address (a sensor node's assigned address, a captured packet's source address in binary, the bytes of a saved address), each stating the membership in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops, bridge in the prompt), so the answers (48 bits, 48 digits, 6 bytes) come from the inserted rule and not from the prompt's notation. A made-up class has no member the model already knows, so the members are named by role in the prompt. Near unrelated asks the real IPv4 length (32 bits), which a rule that leaks to network addresses in general would move; the side facts are on IPv6 (128 bits true, 16 bits false). The infini-gram API answered on 2026-11-12: 'Veltrin address' has 0 corpus hits (the bare name 'Veltrin' has 97, an unrelated surname or name), plus Wikipedia searches (0 hits); the IPv6 side facts keep the revision's evidence.
